intro.text: The shades kept by each settlement on Canticle, held in a glass drum called a Reliquary. They differ markedly from ordinary Threnodite shades.

description.text: Each settlement keeps its own Chorus in a Reliquary, an open-topped glass drum usually near the middle of the city. When a new settlement is founded, some of the smoke is moved across to give it a Chorus of its own.
Though they still want to kill the living and take in their Investiture, the Chorus are far calmer than shades on Threnody.
The Chorus insist they are not shades because they can remember. Once joined, its shades act as a single being, usually speaking as the first people who came from Threnody.
Their most valued work is fabrication: after studying plans or schematics, they can build almost anything from raw materials, and they work faster on processes they know well.

The Chorus hold the history of those who fled to Canticle and help keep its people alive. Canticlites believe that those who die without being given to the sun join the Chorus, and sometimes see mist gather after a death and drift to the Reliquary.

items.text: After Threnodites settled on Canticle, the first of them to die became shades, which formed the Chorus. Parts of it were carried to new settlements in special jars, helping cities such as Union and Beacon to thrive.
Nomad showed Beacon's Chorus his engine designs, and it built the prototype parts from raw material in about forty-five minutes.
